source_pdfs.label: Animation and Motion Graphics 2-Year Degree Map
Animation and Motion Graphics 5-Semester Degree Map

faculty_override_note: The official two-year, four-semester map is the default. The official five-semester map is an alternate lighter-load pathway. DegreeWorks and faculty advisement remain authoritative.
sequence_notes: This program's own page describes the generic, boilerplate 12/18/30 Common-Core/Flexible-Core/Curriculum-Requirements split used across most BMCC AA/AS programs. It does not match this degree map, which has no separate Individual and Society, Scientific World, or World Cultures slots -- those Pathways areas are entirely replaced by specific required program courses, the same pattern already found for Video Arts and Technology (this program's sibling major in the same department).

Required Common Core is declared at 13 credits (not the usual nominal 12), matching the literal sum of its own courses (ENG 101 3 + ENG 201 3 + MAT 161 3 + PHY 110 4). Unlike other majors, this program has no separate General Elective placeholder to absorb PHY 110's one-credit STEM excess, so Common Core absorbs it directly -- confirmed by reconciling every course and credit value on both official maps to exactly 60.

Select any Creative Expression Pathways course except SPE 100, SPE 102, OR MES 153 for the second Creative Expression requirement -- a three-way exclusion (not the usual two-way SPE 100/SPE 102 exclusion), because MES 153 is itself a Pathways-eligible Creative Expression course that is already separately required as a fixed Program Requirement.

MMP 100 and MMA 100 chain: MMP 250 requires MMP 100; ANI 260 and ANI 401 both require MMP 100 or MMA 100 per the official course-listings page. This program's own degree-map footnote instead states an AND relationship ('MMP 100 and MMA 100 must be passed'), which conflicts with the catalog. The catalog's OR was used, both because it is the more authoritative registrar-facing source and to stay consistent with the identical ANI 401 encoding already established in vat_as_courses.csv.

ANI 301's official title is 'Introduction to Motion Graphics and Visual Effects' (confirmed twice against the course-listings page) and its prerequisite is 'VAT 161 or VAT 171 or MMA 100 or MMP 100' -- both exactly matching the ANI 301 row already in vat_as_courses.csv. This program's own degree map mislabels the course as 'Introduction to Video Graphics', which is actually VAT 301/MMP 301's title, not ANI 301's. The course-listings page's title and prerequisite were used instead of the map's incorrect wording (lesson 2). Flagged for maintainer review as an apparent copy-paste error in the official degree map.

ANI 402's official course-listing prerequisite is only 'ANI 401' (with ENG 101 and a MAT 100-level-or-higher course as corequisites, not prerequisites). This program's own degree-map footnote instead states a stricter three-part prerequisite ('ANI 401, MMP 250 and a college-level MAT course'). Given the map's footnote 2 was already found to overstate an AND-relationship the catalog shows as OR (see above), the catalog's simpler, single-course prerequisite was used for ANI 402 too, for internal consistency. The map's additional MMP 250 and 'college-level MAT course' conditions, and the catalog's ENG 101/MAT-level corequisites, are documented but not enforced -- the MAT-level condition is not a specific course code and cannot be encoded regardless. Flagged for maintainer review.

ANI 360 ('2D Animation Projects') is modeled as a reciprocal alternative to ANI 402 per footnote 7 ('ANI 360 is an alternative option'). Unlike SPE 100/SPE 102 or MEA 371/MEA 201, ANI 360 has its own distinct prerequisite (MMP 260 or ANI 260, not ANI 401) rather than an identical one -- the alternatives mechanism still applies correctly since each course's own prerequisite gate is independently enforced regardless of the alternative relationship.

MEA 371 / MEA 201: MEA 201 is an alternate option per footnote 8. Modeled as two reciprocal rows, matching the identical pattern already used in vat_as_courses.csv. MEA 201's own prerequisite ('ANI 401 or two 200-level-or-higher MMA/MMP courses') is not encoded -- the 'any two of a pool' condition has no primitive in the current prerequisite grammar, same limitation already documented for VAT_AS.

The 'ANI Elective' concept (footnote 3): MMP 250 is described as satisfying an implicit ANI-elective requirement, with MMA 215, MMA 225, MMA 235, MMP 210, ANI 301, COM 240, COM 245, MEA 211, MEA 371, MEA 300, HED 250, or BUS 200 as officially interchangeable alternatives. This was NOT modeled as a flexible choice group or as `alternatives` on MMP 250, because two of those alternates (ANI 301, MEA 371) are already separately, independently required elsewhere on this same map -- linking them as alternatives to MMP 250 via the graph-based `alternativeComponents()` mechanism would incorrectly merge three genuinely distinct requirements into one shared slot. MMP 250 is modeled as the literal, fixed course shown on the map; the official substitution flexibility is documented here but not enforced. Flagged for maintainer review.

ART 176 is listed as an alternate to ART 269 (footnote 4), but its title and credits could not be verified -- the Art & Design department's course-listings page returned repeated HTTP 503 errors. Not added as a row rather than guessed at. Flagged for maintainer review.
A Writing Intensive course is required for graduation.
